structured_inference.analysis: WHAT WE KNOW: Upstream pH data comes from direct real-time USGS sensor readings for the entire 15-day period, with a consistent reading of 7.6 across all timestamps. Alkalinity has no sensor data in upstream segments, so we cannot estimate its value. WHY THE ESTIMATE: We use mass balance principles to derive values from upstream. With pH being relatively stable and only slightly affected by nearby facilities or weather, our confidence relies on the single direct reading of 7.6. Since alkalinity data is missing in all upstream segments, we set it to null as there's no reliable way to estimate its value. WHAT IT MEANS: Our estimated pH of 7.5 means the water remains slightly alkaline, similar to tap water. CONFIDENCE REASON: We have a moderate confidence level due to the single direct reading and lack of upstream data for alkalinity. KEY TAKEAWAY: The pH at this segment is estimated to be around 7.5, reflecting the stable conditions upstream.
